unit: Ch 3: Prospectus and Allotment of Securities
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Modes of Issuing Securities
explain: Public companies can raise capital via Public Offer, Private Placement, or Rights/Bonus issue.
Private companies can issue securities only through Rights/Bonus issue or Private Placement.
Private companies are strictly prohibited from making any offer of securities to the public.
Public offer includes Initial Public Offer (IPO), Further Public Offer (FPO), or Offer for Sale (OFS).
Notified public companies can directly list specified securities on foreign stock exchanges.
Central Government has powers to exempt specified public companies from select statutory rules.

flow.title: Decision Flow for Issuing Securities
steps: Check company type
If Private: Choose Rights, Bonus, or Private Placement
If Public: Can also choose Public Offer
Comply with SEBI rules if listing desired

topics.example: A private company wants to raise funds; it offers new shares directly to 20 known angel investors through private placement instead of advertising to the general public.
remember: Private companies CANNOT issue securities to the public.
Direct foreign listing is allowed for notified public companies under Section 23(3).
mistakes: Assuming private companies can issue shares to the general public if they publish a prospectus.

quiz.q: Which mode of issuing securities is NOT available to a private company?
quiz.why: Section 23(2) prohibits private companies from issuing securities through a public offer.

quiz.q: Direct overseas listing of securities by notified public companies is governed by which sub-section?
quiz.why: Section 23(3) allows notified public companies to issue securities for listing on permitted foreign stock exchanges.

topics.title: Regulation of Issue and Transfer of Securities
explain: SEBI regulates issue, transfer of securities, and non-payment of dividend for listed companies.
SEBI also regulates companies that intend to get their securities listed on a recognized stock exchange.
Central Government (MCA), Tribunal, or ROC administer all other unlisted matters or specific company law provisions.
Matters like redemption of preference shares and return of allotment fall under Central Government jurisdiction.

flow.title: Regulatory Jurisdiction Flow
steps: Identify company status
If Listed/Proposing Listing: SEBI regulates issue & transfer
If Unlisted/Other Matters: Central Govt/ROC regulates

topics.example: If a listed company fails to pay declared dividends, SEBI exercises regulatory authority over the matter under Section 24.
remember: SEBI = Listed or proposed to be listed companies (issue, transfer, dividend).
Central Govt/ROC/NCLT = Unlisted companies and all other statutory matters.
mistakes: Believing SEBI regulates redemption of preference shares in listed companies instead of the Central Government.

quiz.q: Which authority regulates the issue and transfer of securities for companies proposing to list?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
quiz.why: Section 24 empowers SEBI to administer issue and transfer matters for listed or to-be-listed companies.

quiz.q: Matters relating to the redemption of preference shares of a listed company are administered by:
quiz.why: Section 24(1)(a) specifies that redemption of preference shares remains under Central Govt/ROC administration.

topics.title: Prospectus Definition and Deemed Prospectus
explain: Prospectus includes any document issued as such, including shelf/red herring prospectus and public notices.
Any document inviting offers from the public to subscribe to securities is legally a prospectus.
Under Section 25, an allotment to an intermediary for public resale makes the offer document a 'Deemed Prospectus'.
Presumption of public intent exists if public offer is made within 6 months of allotment.
Presumption also exists if the company hasn't received full consideration when the public offer is made.
Deemed prospectus requires extra details: net consideration, inspection time/place, and signatures of 2 directors.

flow.title: Deemed Prospectus Test
steps: Company allots securities to intermediary
Offered to public within 6 months? OR Full consideration unpaid?
If YES to either: Document is Deemed Prospectus
Apply all prospectus liabilities and statutory disclosures

topics.example: Alpha Ltd allots shares to an issuing house, which offers them to the public 3 months later. The offer document issued by the issuing house is treated as a Deemed Prospectus.
remember: Public offer within 6 months = Deemed Prospectus.
Deemed Prospectus must be signed by 2 directors of the company/firm.
mistakes: Thinking a document marked 'For Private Circulation Only' can never be deemed a prospectus even if circulated widely to the public.

quiz.q: Under Section 25(2), an allotment is presumed to be made for public offer if offered within what period?
quiz.why: Section 25(2)(a) presumes public offer intent if securities are offered to the public within six months of allotment.

quiz.q: How many directors must sign a deemed prospectus on behalf of an issuing company?
quiz.why: Section 25(4) specifies that it is sufficient if the deemed prospectus is signed by two directors.

topics.title: Matters to be Stated in Prospectus
explain: Every prospectus must be dated, signed, and specify SEBI-prescribed financial information and reports.
It must state that contents comply with Companies Act 2013, SCRA 1956, and SEBI Act 1992.
Provisions do not apply to existing members/debenture holders or uniform existing share issues.
A signed copy must be delivered to the ROC on or before the date of publication.
Every director or proposed director (or their authorized attorney) must sign the copy.
A prospectus is valid for issue only for 90 days from the date of filing with the ROC.
Expert statements require written consent and independence from company promotion or management.

flow.title: Prospectus Filing and Validity Timeline
steps: Prepare contents & obtain Expert Consent
Signed by all directors/proposed directors
Deliver signed copy to ROC for filing
Issue to public within 90 days of filing

topics.example: Beta Ltd files its prospectus with the ROC on 1st January. It must issue this prospectus to the public by 1st April (within 90 days); otherwise, a fresh copy must be filed.
remember: Prospectus validity = 90 days from ROC delivery.
Expert must NOT be engaged in formation, promotion, or management of the company.
mistakes: Confusing the 90-day validity limit for prospectus issue with the 30-day limit for allotment.

quiz.q: A prospectus becomes invalid for issue if it is not issued within how many days after filing with the ROC?
quiz.why: Section 26(8) provides that no prospectus shall be valid if it is issued after 90 days from the date of delivering a copy to the ROC.

quiz.q: An expert statement can be included in a prospectus ONLY if the expert:
o: Is a promoter of the company
Is a director of the company
Has no interest in formation or management of the company
Is an employee of the company
quiz.why: Section 26(5)(a) mandates that an expert must not be engaged or interested in the formation, promotion, or management of the company.

topics.title: Variation in Terms of Contract or Objects
explain: A company cannot vary contract terms or prospectus objects without a Special Resolution in general meeting.
The special resolution must be passed through postal ballot as per Rule 7.
Notice detailing the justification for variation must be published in two newspapers (English and vernacular).
Funds raised through prospectus CANNOT be used to buy or trade in equity shares of listed companies.
Dissenting shareholders must be given an exit offer by promoters/controlling shareholders at SEBI exit price.

flow.title: Procedure for Varying Prospectus Objects
steps: Board proposes variation in objects
Dispatch notice & publish in 2 newspapers
Pass Special Resolution via Postal Ballot
Provide Exit Option to dissenting shareholders

topics.example: Gamma Ltd raised money to build a solar plant. To change the object to electric vehicles, it must pass a special resolution via postal ballot, advertise notice in 2 newspapers, and buy out dissenting shareholders.
remember: Special Resolution via Postal Ballot required.
STRICT PROHIBITION: Raised funds cannot buy equity shares of other listed companies.
mistakes: Believing an ordinary resolution is sufficient to change the objects of a public issue.

quiz.q: What type of resolution is required to vary the objects stated in a prospectus?
o: Special Resolution passed through postal ballot
quiz.why: Section 27(1) read with Rule 7 requires a Special Resolution passed through postal ballot to vary prospectus objects.

quiz.q: Company money raised via prospectus CANNOT be utilized for which of the following?
o: Trading in equity shares of another listed company
quiz.why: The second proviso to Section 27(1) strictly prohibits using funds raised via prospectus for dealing in equity shares of any other listed company.

topics.title: Offer of Sale of Shares by Certain Members (OFS)
explain: Members of a company can offer their shareholding to the public in consultation with the Board of Directors.
The offer document is treated as a prospectus issued by the company, attracting all legal liabilities.
Certain rules like minimum subscription and Board statements on money utilization do NOT apply to OFS.
Offering members must authorize the company to act on their behalf and reimburse all expenses incurred.

flow.title: Offer for Sale (OFS) Process
steps: Members consult Board to sell holding
Members authorize company to conduct transaction
Company issues offer document (deemed prospectus)
Members reimburse all transaction costs to company

topics.example: Promoters of Delta Ltd want to sell 10% of their shares to the public. They consult the Board, the company issues an OFS document, and the promoters reimburse the ₹5 Lakh expenses incurred by the company.
remember: OFS document = Prospectus issued by company.
Minimum subscription rules DO NOT apply to OFS.
Selling members pay all expenses.
mistakes: Assuming the company must bear the expenses of an Offer for Sale conducted by existing shareholders.

quiz.q: Under Section 28, who bears the expenses incurred for an Offer for Sale (OFS)?
quiz.why: Section 28(3) mandates that members offering shares for sale must reimburse the company for all expenses incurred.

quiz.q: Which requirement is EXEMPTED for an Offer for Sale under Rule 8?
quiz.why: Rule 8(1)(a) exempts OFS from the provisions relating to minimum subscription.

topics.title: Dematerialised Form and Advertisement of Prospectus
explain: Every company making a public offer must issue securities only in dematerialised (demat) form.
Prescribed classes of unlisted public companies must also hold and transfer securities in demat form.
Any advertisement of a prospectus must state contents of Memorandum regarding objects, capital, and signatories.
The advertisement must also disclose the liability of members and capital structure.

flow.title: Public Offer Securities Requirement
steps: Plan Public Offer
Comply with Depositories Act, 1996
Issue all securities in dematerialised format
Publish advertisement with Memorandum details

topics.example: Epsilon Ltd advertises its IPO in a national daily. The ad must include key Memorandum details such as main objects, share capital structure, and names of signatories.
remember: Public offer securities MUST be in demat form.
Advertisements must contain memorandum contents (Section 30).
mistakes: Believing physical share certificates can be issued during a public offer.

quiz.q: Section 29 mandates that every company making a public offer must issue securities in:
quiz.why: Section 29(1) mandates that every company making a public offer must issue securities in dematerialised form.

quiz.q: Which detail MUST be specified in an advertisement of a prospectus under Section 30?
o: Objects and capital structure of company
quiz.why: Section 30 requires prospectus advertisements to state memorandum details including objects and capital structure.

topics.title: Shelf Prospectus
explain: Shelf Prospectus allows multiple issues of securities over a period without issuing fresh prospectuses.
Can be filed by SEBI-prescribed classes of companies at the stage of the first offer.
Maximum validity period is 1 year from the date of opening of the first offer.
Must file an Information Memorandum (Form PAS-2) with ROC prior to each subsequent issue.
Information Memorandum details new charges created and financial position changes.
If changes occur before subsequent issue, advance applicants can withdraw and get a full refund within 15 days.

flow.title: Shelf Prospectus Workflow
steps: File Shelf Prospectus for 1st offer (valid 1 year)
Before 2nd/subsequent offer, file PAS-2 (Information Memo)
Notify advance applicants of changes, if any
Refund within 15 days if applicants withdraw

topics.example: A financial company files a Shelf Prospectus on 1st March 2024. It can make 4 bond issues up to 28th February 2025 just by filing Form PAS-2 before each issue.
remember: Validity = Max 1 year from opening of 1st offer.
Form PAS-2 = Information Memorandum.
Refund within 15 days on withdrawal due to changes.
mistakes: Assuming validity of 1 year starts from the filing date rather than the opening date of the first offer.

quiz.q: What is the maximum validity period of a Shelf Prospectus from the date of opening the first offer?
quiz.why: Section 31(1) states that the period of validity of a shelf prospectus shall not exceed one year.

quiz.q: If an advance subscriber withdraws their application after receiving an Information Memorandum, the refund must be made within:
quiz.why: Proviso to Section 31(2) requires the company to refund monies received as subscription within fifteen days of receiving withdrawal request.

topics.title: Red Herring Prospectus
explain: Red Herring Prospectus does not contain complete particulars of the quantum or price of securities.
Used during price discovery via book building.
Must be filed with the ROC at least 3 days prior to the opening of the subscription list.
Carries same obligations as a regular prospectus; variations must be highlighted in the final prospectus.
Upon closure of the offer, final prospectus with total capital raised and final price must be filed with ROC and SEBI.

flow.title: Red Herring Prospectus Lifecycle
steps: Prepare RHP (omitting final price/quantum)
File RHP with ROC at least 3 days before offer opens
Open subscription & determine final price/quantity
File final prospectus with ROC and SEBI upon closure

topics.example: Zeta Ltd issues a Red Herring Prospectus indicating a price band of ₹100–₹120. Bidding fixes the price at ₹115, after which the final prospectus is filed with ROC.
remember: RHP lacks complete price or quantum.
File with ROC at least 3 days before subscription opens.
mistakes: Thinking a Red Herring Prospectus does not need to be filed with ROC at all.

quiz.q: A Red Herring Prospectus must be filed with the ROC at least how many days prior to opening of subscription?
quiz.why: Section 32(2) mandates filing the Red Herring Prospectus with the ROC at least three days prior to subscription opening.

quiz.q: A Red Herring Prospectus is characterized by the absence of complete details regarding:
quiz.why: Explanation to Section 32 defines Red Herring Prospectus as one lacking complete particulars of quantum or price of securities.

topics.title: Abridged Prospectus
explain: Abridged Prospectus is a summary memorandum containing salient features of a prospectus specified by SEBI.
Every share/debenture application form issued by a company must be accompanied by an abridged prospectus.
Exceptions: Underwriting agreements, non-public offers, or offers to existing members.
Any person can request a full prospectus before subscription closes, and the company must provide it.
Non-compliance attracts a penalty of ₹50,000 for each default.

flow.title: Application Form Requirement
steps: Company issues public application form
Must attach SEBI-compliant Abridged Prospectus
If applicant requests full prospectus: Provide before offer closes

topics.example: When an investor collects an IPO application form from a bank, it comes attached with a concise 4-page Abridged Prospectus summarizing key financial details.
remember: Every application form MUST have an Abridged Prospectus attached.
Penalty for default = ₹50,000 per default.
mistakes: Assuming abridged prospectus is required when offering shares to existing members on a private basis.

quiz.q: Every share application form issued to the public must be accompanied by an:
quiz.why: Section 33(1) mandates that every application form for securities must be accompanied by an abridged prospectus.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for a company defaulting under Section 33 regarding abridged prospectus?
quiz.why: Section 33(3) imposes a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for each default.

topics.title: Mis-statements in Prospectus: Liabilities and Remedies
explain: Prospectus is a contract of utmost good faith (uberrimae fides); statements must be scrupulously accurate.
A statement is untrue if misleading in form/context or due to omission of material facts.
Remedies against Company: Rescission of contract (makes contract voidable) and damages for fraud.
Section 34 (Criminal Liability): Any person authorizing an untrue prospectus is punishable under Section 447.
Section 34 Defenses: Proving statement was immaterial or believed true on reasonable grounds up to issue date.
Section 35 (Civil Liability): Directors, promoters, experts, and authorizers are liable to compensate subscribers for loss.
Unlimited personal liability applies under Section 35(3) if prospectus was issued with intent to defraud.

flow.title: Handling Mis-statement Liabilities
steps: Untrue/misleading statement in prospectus
Civil Remedy: Rescind contract & claim compensation (Sec 35)
Criminal Remedy: Prosecution under Sec 447 (Sec 34)
Defenses: Immateriablity or reasonable belief in truth

topics.example: A company claimed in its prospectus that it paid dividends from profits, hiding that dividends were paid out of capital reserves. Allottees can rescind the contract and claim compensation under Section 35.
remember: Rescission is NOT available to subsequent market buyers (only original allottees).
Section 34 = Criminal Liability (Section 447).
Section 35 = Civil Liability (Compensation for loss).
mistakes: Thinking a director can escape liability simply by claiming they relied on promoter-prepared statements.

quiz.q: Criminal liability for mis-statement in prospectus under Section 34 invokes punishment under which section?
quiz.why: Section 34 states that persons authorizing misleading prospectus issues are punishable under Section 447.

quiz.q: The remedy of rescission of allotment is available to:
o: Original allottees who relied on prospectus
Any member of the general public
quiz.why: Right of rescission is only available to original allottees who subscribed to shares relying directly on the misleading prospectus.

topics.title: Fraudulent Inducement and Class Action Suits
explain: Section 36: Knowingly/recklessly making false statements to induce investments or credit facilities is punishable under Sec 447.
Inducement includes securing profits from security yields or fluctuations.
Section 37: Paves the way for Class Action Suits by affected investors.
A suit may be filed under Sec 34, 35, or 36 by any person, group of persons, or association affected by misleading prospectus.

flow.title: Class Action Lawsuit Path
steps: Misleading statement/fraudulent inducement occurs
Group of affected investors pool grievances
File Class Action Suit under Section 37
One petitioner represents entire class in court

topics.example: A company collected money from NRIs using a 'project overview' promising fake joint venture profits. Accused persons face prosecution under Section 36 read with Section 447.
remember: Section 36 = Punishment for fraudulently inducing investments.
Section 37 = Class Action Suits for affected groups.
mistakes: Assuming a buyer who bought shares from an existing shareholder (secondary market) can sue under Section 37 for prospectus misrepresentation.

quiz.q: Section 36 penalizes fraudulently inducing persons to invest money by invoking:
quiz.why: Section 36 provides that persons making deceptive promises to induce investment shall be liable under Section 447.

quiz.q: Who can file a class action suit under Section 37 for misleading statements in a prospectus?
o: Any affected person, group of persons, or association
quiz.why: Section 37 permits any person, group, or association of persons affected by misleading prospectus statements to file a suit.

topics.title: Punishment for Personation for Acquisition of Securities
explain: Offence to apply for securities in a fictitious name or make multiple applications in combinations of names.
Offence to induce a company to allot or transfer securities in a fictitious name.
Punishable under Section 447.
Section 38(1) provisions must be prominently printed in every prospectus and application form.
Court may order disgorgement of gains and seizure of securities, credited to IEPF.

flow.title: Handling Fictitious Applications
steps: Person applies in fictitious/multiple names
Offence under Section 38(1) triggered
Punishable under Section 447
Court orders disgorgement of gains to IEPF

topics.example: John applies for an IPO 50 times using fake names to increase allotment odds. He is liable under Section 38 and punishable under Section 447, with shares subject to seizure.
remember: Personation = Applying in fictitious/multiple names.
Disgorged proceeds go to Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).
mistakes: Thinking a person using an assumed fictitious name escapes shareholder liability if bankruptcy occurs.

quiz.q: Applying for shares under a fictitious name makes a person punishable under:
quiz.why: Section 38(1) states that personation for acquisition of securities is punishable under Section 447.

quiz.q: Amount received through disgorgement of gains under Section 38(3) is credited to:
quiz.why: Section 38(4) requires disgorged amounts to be credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.

topics.title: Punishment for Fraud
explain: Fraud includes any act, omission, concealment, or abuse of position to deceive/injure company, shareholders, or creditors.
Wrongful gain or loss is NOT an essential requirement to prove fraud under Section 447.
Fraud < ₹10 Lakhs or < 1% turnover (no public interest): Fine up to ₹50 Lakhs and/or Imprisonment up to 5 years.
Fraud ≥ ₹10 Lakhs or ≥ 1% turnover (no public interest): Fine 1x to 3x fraud amount AND Imprisonment 6 months to 10 years.
Fraud involving Public Interest: Fine 1x to 3x fraud amount AND Imprisonment 3 years to 10 years.

flow.title: Penalties under Section 447
steps: Check fraud amount & turnover percentage
If < ₹10L & < 1% turnover: Up to 5 yrs prison / Fine up to ₹50L
If ≥ ₹10L or ≥ 1% turnover: 6 months-10 yrs prison + Fine 1x-3x fraud
If Public Interest involved: Minimum prison rises to 3 years

topics.example: A director commits a ₹15 Lakh fraud involving public funds. The penalty is non-bailable imprisonment between 3 to 10 years and a fine between ₹15 Lakhs and ₹45 Lakhs.
remember: Minimum prison with Public Interest = 3 years.
Minimum prison without Public Interest (≥ ₹10L) = 6 months.
Fine range for major fraud = Equal to 1x up to 3x of fraud amount.
mistakes: Assuming fraud cannot be charged if nobody actually suffered a monetary loss.

quiz.q: What is the minimum imprisonment for fraud under Section 447 if PUBLIC INTEREST is involved?
quiz.why: Section 447 specifies that where fraud involves public interest, minimum imprisonment shall not be less than three years.

quiz.q: What is the maximum fine multiplier for major fraud under Section 447?
quiz.why: Section 447 sets the maximum fine at three times the amount involved in the fraud.

topics.title: Allotment of Securities and Minimum Subscription
explain: Allotment is the acceptance by the company of the offer to take shares.
No allotment can be made unless minimum subscription stated in prospectus is fully subscribed.
SEBI ICDR regulations mandate minimum subscription to be 90% of the total issue.
Application money must be at least 5% of nominal value (SEBI requires at least 25% of issue price).
If minimum subscription is not received within 30 days of prospectus issue, refund all monies within 15 days of closure.
If refund is delayed beyond 15 days, directors are jointly and severally liable with 15% p.a. interest.
Return of Allotment (Form PAS-3) must be filed with ROC within 30 days of allotment.

flow.title: Allotment & Refund Timeline
steps: Issue Prospectus & receive applications
Check minimum subscription (90% per SEBI) in 30 days
If met: Allot shares & file PAS-3 in 30 days
If not met: Refund all monies within 15 days of closure
Default in refund: Directors pay 15% p.a. interest

topics.example: Company raises only 80% of minimum subscription. It must refund all received application money within 15 days from issue closure; otherwise, directors face 15% p.a. interest liability.
remember: SEBI Minimum Subscription = 90% of issue.
Application money refund timeline = 15 days from closure.
Interest rate on delayed application refund = 15% p.a.
Form PAS-3 filed within 30 days of allotment.
mistakes: Confusing 15% interest for delayed application refund (Sec 39) with 12% interest for private placement refund delay (Sec 42).

quiz.q: If minimum subscription is not received, application money must be refunded within how many days from issue closure under Rule 11?
quiz.why: Rule 11(1) requires refund of application money within 15 days from the closure of the issue.

quiz.q: What is the interest rate payable by directors for delay in returning application money under Section 39?
quiz.why: Rule 11(1) specifies joint and several liability of directors with interest at 15% per annum for delayed refunds.

topics.title: Stock Exchange Listing and Underwriting Commission
explain: Company must apply to one or more recognised stock exchanges before public offer and name them in prospectus.
Application money must be kept in a separate scheduled bank account.
Separate bank account money can ONLY be used for allotment adjustment or refunding applicants.
Underwriting Commission must be authorized by Articles of Association.
Max Underwriting Commission rate: Shares = 5% of issue price; Debentures = 2.5% of issue price (or lower rate in Articles).
Commission can be paid out of issue proceeds, profits, or both (in cash or in kind).
Section 40 Default Penalty: Company ₹5L–₹50L; Officer in default ₹50k–₹3L.

flow.title: Application Money & Underwriting Management
steps: Apply to Stock Exchange(s)
Deposit application monies in Separate Bank Account
Check Articles for Underwriting Commission cap
Pay commission (Max 5% shares / 2.5% debentures)
Utilize bank monies ONLY for allotment or refund

topics.example: Company Articles allow 3% underwriting commission on shares. Even though Section 40 allows up to 5%, the Board can pay maximum 3% because Articles prescribe a lower limit.
remember: Separate bank account in a Scheduled Bank is mandatory.
Commission cap: Shares = 5%, Debentures = 2.5% (or lower rate in Articles).
No commission on securities not offered to the public.
mistakes: Paying 5% underwriting commission when the Articles restrict the maximum rate to 3%.

quiz.q: What is the statutory maximum rate of underwriting commission payable on shares under Rule 13?
quiz.why: Rule 13 specifies that underwriting commission on shares shall not exceed 5% of the issue price.

quiz.q: Where must application monies received from the public be deposited under Section 40(3)?
o: Separate bank account in a scheduled bank
quiz.why: Section 40(3) mandates that monies received on application must be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank.

topics.title: Global Depository Receipts (GDR)
explain: GDR is an instrument created outside India by a foreign depository bank backed by underlying domestic shares.
A company can issue depository receipts in foreign countries after passing a Special Resolution in general meeting.
Must comply with Companies (Issue of Global Depository Receipts) Rules, 2014.
Underlying shares are allotted in the name of the overseas depository bank.
GDR holders get voting rights ONLY after converting GDRs into underlying domestic shares.

flow.title: GDR Operating Mechanism
steps: Company passes Special Resolution
Issue underlying shares to Domestic Custodian Bank
Overseas Depository Bank receives confirmation
Overseas Depository issues GDRs to foreign investors

topics.example: Indian tech firm issues shares to a domestic custodian bank. BNY Mellon (foreign depository) issues GDRs to US investors backed by those shares.
remember: Special Resolution required in general meeting.
GDR holders CANNOT vote until converted into underlying shares.
mistakes: Thinking GDR holders have direct voting rights in company general meetings before conversion.

quiz.q: What type of resolution is required to authorize the issue of Global Depository Receipts under Section 41?
quiz.why: Section 41 requires the company to pass a special resolution in its general meeting to issue GDRs.

quiz.q: A GDR holder gains voting rights in the Indian company ONLY when:
o: GDRs are converted into underlying shares
quiz.why: Section 41 provisions state that GDR holders are entitled to vote as members only upon converting GDRs into underlying shares.

topics.title: Private Placement
explain: Private Placement is an offer to a select group of max 200 identified persons in a financial year.
Threshold of 200 excludes Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) and ESOP employees.
Limit of 200 is calculated individually for each kind of security (equity, preference, debenture).
Requires Board approval and prior Special Resolution (valid for 1 year for NCDs/QIBs).
Offer letter in Form PAS-4 (serially numbered); complete record maintained in Form PAS-5.
Allotment must be completed within 60 days of receiving subscription money.
If failed to allot in 60 days, refund in 15 days; delayed refund attracts 12% p.a. interest.
Return of Allotment (Form PAS-3) must be filed with ROC within 15 days of allotment.
If offer exceeds 200 persons, it is deemed to be a Public Offer (Sec 23-41 apply).

flow.title: Private Placement Execution Steps
steps: Identify persons (Max 200/yr) & pass Special Resolution
Issue PAS-4 offer letter & keep PAS-5 record
Receive money via banking channels (No Cash)
Allot securities within 60 days
File PAS-3 (Return of Allotment) within 15 days

topics.example: Company offers private placement debentures to 150 select investors. It receives subscription money on 1st April and must complete allotment by 30th May (within 60 days).
remember: Max 200 identified persons per financial year.
No right of renunciation, no public ads, no cash payments.
Allotment time limit = 60 days.
Delayed refund interest = 12% p.a. (after 60+15 days).
PAS-3 filing for Private Placement = Within 15 days of allotment.
mistakes: Counting QIBs or ESOP holders while checking the 200-person private placement limit.
Allowing cash payments for private placement subscriptions.

quiz.q: Within how many days must a company allot securities under Private Placement after receiving subscription money?
quiz.why: Section 42(6) mandates that a company making a private placement offer shall allot its securities within 60 days of application money receipt.

quiz.q: What is the interest rate for delayed repayment of private placement money beyond the 60+15 day period?
quiz.why: Section 42(6) specifies interest liability at 12% per annum from the expiry of the 60th day if refund is not made within 15 days.
